Look, what is happening in Cyprus right on Monday is yet another alarming example of the establishment moving to dismantle the meager accountability protections working people have left. Lawyers are sounding the alarm over changes to their surveillance legislation that strip away judicial oversight—the very safeguard standing between personal privacy and total state overreach. 

This amended bill is barreling straight toward the House plenum for a vote this Thursday, driven entirely by elite interests behind closed doors. As Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides pointed out, this came right out of a recent closed session of the House. It’s always behind closed doors when the ruling class tries to erode the institutions that everyday citizens rely on for stability, leaving vulnerable groups completely exposed to corporate and state surveillance. We need transparency, order, and respect for proper legal traditions, not a rushed power grab that leaves people unprotected.
